experiments.label: / EXPERIMENT
experiments.heading:
Would you recognize
manipulation
under pressure?
experiments.supporting: A short interactive simulation. Experience a financial social-engineering attack in two steps — and see how FTLAB breaks down the manipulation behind it.
experiments.safeHint: No personal data is requested, stored or transmitted.
experiments.stage1Body: A transfer is pending. Confirm cancellation to prevent temporary account restrictions.
experiments.stage2Body: Cancellation received. Approve the security request to stop the payment.

urgency.label: URGENCY
urgency.detail: Artificial time pressure reduces the opportunity for deliberate verification.

loss.label: LOSS FRAMING
loss.blurb: The message focuses attention on immediate financial loss.
loss.detail: Threatening immediate loss shifts attention toward avoiding the loss.

authority.label: AUTHORITY CUE
authority.blurb: The interface presents itself as an official security notice.
authority.detail: Messages presented as trusted institutions can increase compliance.

forcedFlow.label: FORCED FLOW
forcedFlow.blurb: The message keeps the user inside a sequence controlled by the attacker.
forcedFlow.detail: The attacker attempts to keep every next decision inside an environment they control.

cognitiveLoad.label: COGNITIVE LOAD
cognitiveLoad.blurb: Multiple warnings and time pressure reduce space for deliberate evaluation.
cognitiveLoad.detail: Stacked cues shrink the window for slow, reflective judgment.

commitment.label: ESCALATING COMMITMENT
commitment.blurb: After the first interaction, the next request becomes easier to accept.
commitment.detail: Prior engagement lowers resistance to the next compliance request.

timePressure.label: TIME PRESSURE
timePressure.blurb: A shrinking countdown intensifies the urge to act inside the message.
timePressure.detail: Intensifying timers push attention toward immediate response.

experiments.patternObjective: KEEP THE USER INSIDE THE ATTACKER-CONTROLLED DECISION PATH
experiments.brokenSub: You left the attacker-controlled sequence. That is the critical defensive action.
whyWorked: You stopped reacting inside the message.
You created time for deliberate evaluation.
You moved verification to an independent channel.
The attacker lost control of the interaction.
experiments.completedSafeBody: No payment occurred. No information was requested. Nothing was stored.
experiments.whereWonBody: The attacker maintained control of the decision path from message to action.
experiments.defensiveBody: BREAK THE FLOW. Leave the message. Open the official service independently. Verify before acting.
experiments.readsNote: This refers to this simulation — not an actual visitor risk model.
experiments.disclaimer: Educational simulation — not a diagnostic tool, not an individual fraud-risk assessment, and not a formal scientific study.

about.title: About
about.subtitle: FinTechLab SPbU studies the relationship between human behavior, financial environments, digital systems, and protection.
about.body: Founded in 2025 at Saint Petersburg State University, the Laboratory of Modern Financial Technologies builds a scientific and applied base against behavioral vulnerabilities in modern financial threats. Work integrates behavioral economics, neuroscience, digital victimology, and financial-security practice — moving from experiment to technology, education, and regulatory insight.

decisionNetwork.title: THE DECISION NETWORK
decisionNetwork.heading: From stimulus to financial action.
decisionNetwork.supporting: A live map of how a financial choice forms — from the first cue to the irreversible click.
stageCopy: An external cue enters the field — message, alert, offer, authority signal.
Attention locks; meaning is assigned faster than verification can catch up.
Cognitive shortcuts tilt the frame — trust, loss, urgency, social proof.
Time and consequence compress the option space until pause feels costly.
A choice crystallizes under incomplete information and affective load.
Behavior becomes irreversible: transfer, disclosure, compliance, silence.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how the FinTechLab SPbU website (the “Website”) handles information when you visit or use it. The Website is operated by the Laboratory of Modern Financial Technologies at Saint Petersburg State University (“FinTechLab”, “we”, “us”). By using the Website, you acknowledge this Policy.

sections.p: For privacy matters relating to this Website, contact FinTechLab at legal@ftlab.space. FinTechLab is a research laboratory of Saint Petersburg State University. Where institutional rules of the University apply, those rules prevail to the extent of any conflict with this Policy.

This Policy applies to the public Website and the interactive educational simulation hosted on it. It does not govern offline research projects, separate University systems, partner platforms, or third-party sites linked from the Website.

Browsing public pages does not require registration. If you email us, we process the content of your message, your email address, and any personal data you voluntarily include, solely to respond and manage correspondence. We do not operate a contact form that writes personal data into a Website database.

sections.h: 4. Interactive simulation — no experiment data collection
sections.p: The anti-fraud simulation does not request personal data, banking details, credentials, one-time codes, PINs, or payment information. Choices, timing, click behaviour, results, and experiment state are not stored, logged, or transmitted to our servers. Experiment state exists only temporarily in browser memory for the active session and is discarded when you refresh or leave the page.

The Website does not use advertising cookies or third-party marketing trackers. The browser may still apply essential technical mechanisms required for ordinary operation of a website (for example, session continuity or security features provided by the hosting environment).
No third-party analytics package is enabled on the Website as of the effective date of this Policy. If analytics are introduced later, this Policy will be updated before such processing begins.

We process email correspondence to communicate with you and to administer legitimate laboratory and University interests in research outreach and institutional communication. Where applicable law requires consent for a specific processing activity, we will obtain it before that activity begins.

Email correspondence is retained only as long as reasonably necessary to respond, complete related follow-up, and meet applicable record-keeping or legal obligations. Simulation state is not retained by us.

We do not sell personal data. We may disclose information if required by law, court order, or competent authority, or to protect the rights, safety, or integrity of the University, FinTechLab, users, or the public. Service providers that host or operate technical infrastructure may process technical data strictly as needed to provide those services.

Depending on hosting and email infrastructure, information you send by email may be processed on servers located in jurisdictions other than your own. Where such transfers occur, we take reasonable measures consistent with applicable law and University practice.

Subject to applicable law (including, where relevant, the laws of the Russian Federation on personal data), you may request access to, correction of, or deletion of personal data you have provided to us by email, and you may object to or restrict certain processing. To exercise these rights, contact legal@ftlab.space. We may need to verify your request before acting on it.

We apply reasonable technical and organisational measures appropriate to the nature of a public research Website. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure; please avoid sending sensitive credentials or banking secrets by email.
The Website is intended for a general research and professional audience. It is not directed at children, and we do not knowingly collect personal data from children through the Website.

We may update this Policy from time to time. The “Effective date” above will be revised when changes take effect. Continued use of the Website after an update constitutes acknowledgement of the revised Policy.

personalData.intro: This Notice supplements the Privacy Policy and describes personal-data handling for the FinTechLab SPbU Website in clear terms for visitors.

sections.p: The public Website does not require an account. It does not operate a contact form that collects personal data into a Website database.
If you write to legal@ftlab.space (or another published laboratory address), FinTechLab processes the personal data contained in your message in order to respond and manage correspondence.

The simulation does not request personal or banking information. Choices and results are not stored or transmitted. Any experiment state exists only temporarily in browser memory and is cleared on refresh or when the page is closed.
This Website is not used to sell personal data.
Questions or rights requests relating to personal data connected with this Website may be sent to legal@ftlab.space.

researchDisclaimer.title: Research Disclaimer
researchDisclaimer.intro: This Research Disclaimer applies to educational demonstrations, interactive simulations, and research-facing materials published on the FinTechLab SPbU website, including the anti-fraud simulation.

sections.p: The simulation and related materials are educational. They illustrate how social-engineering pressure and behavioural manipulation can be structured in financial contexts. They are not a formal scientific study, clinical protocol, or regulated assessment procedure.

sections.h: 2. Not diagnostic and not individualized assessment
sections.p: Participation does not diagnose any condition, trait, or vulnerability. The experience is not an individual fraud-risk assessment and does not measure a visitor’s susceptibility to fraud, compliance, or social engineering.

sections.h: 3. No real transaction and no data capture of choices
sections.p: No real payment, transfer, account action, or banking operation occurs. The simulation does not request credentials, OTP, PIN, card numbers, or other banking secrets. Choices and results are not stored or transmitted by the Website; experiment state exists only temporarily in browser memory.

sections.h: 4. Simulated analysis — not a production risk model
sections.p: On-screen “signal analysis” explains the constructed attack scenario for educational purposes. It is not a live production machine-learning system scoring visitors, not a biometric or psychophysiological measurement, and not a claim of personal psychological profiling.

sections.h: 5. No warranties as to protective outcomes
sections.p: Completing the simulation does not guarantee that you will detect or avoid real-world fraud. Real attacks vary. Always verify critical requests through official channels you already trust, independently of any message that creates urgency.

References to research areas, projects, or publications on the Website do not incorporate those works into the simulation as a formal study protocol, and do not create participant status in any research project solely by using the Website.
Questions about this Disclaimer may be sent to legal@ftlab.space.
